target_customer: Congressional offices first, then federal, state and local government agencies
problem: Government staff work across fragmented systems for constituent mail, casework and tasks. Caucus pitched an AI layer that centralizes inboxes and automates responses.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to government offices; pricing not found
product_category: Government CRM and constituent services AI

founders.name: Amir Farahani
previous_startups: Turbo Legi (AI legislative solutions, acquired by FiscalNote)
founders.background_notes: YC launch post says he sold Turbo Legi before finishing undergrad.

founders.name: Tyler Chen
prior_employers: Unnamed Series D startup (AI voice tools)
education: Yale, physics and computer science (student per launch post)
founders.background_notes: Machine learning labs and quantum computing research per the launch post. The two grew up together.

exit.reason: YC lists the company as Inactive; no shutdown notice or cause found. The company site was still live in the fetch.

technical_complexity.rationale: LLM triage and drafting over email, webforms and mail is standard AI engineering, but integrating with House and Senate correspondence systems and meeting security expectations (the site mentions SOC 2 Type II in progress) is harder.

defensibility.rationale: Constituent data sits in entrenched vendor systems, so integration could create switching costs, but a two person team had no demonstrated lock-in and AI drafting features are easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established congressional CRM vendors existed and a December 2025 House hearing described AI tools struggling to plug into existing correspondence management systems. No documented copy or purchase of Caucus.

market_need_then: Congressional offices handle heavy constituent mail and casework. The House Digital Service testimony of December 2025 describes GenAI already helping with form letters and a small pool of vendors holding constituent data. Caucus's own claim of cutting response times from 45 days to seconds is unverified marketing.

branding.domain_note: Uses getcaucus.com as main domain and usecaucus.com for congressional products, per the YC page; no exact .com.

identity.voice_and_tone: bold: 'the last piece of software the American government will ever need', 'Cursor for government'

brand_strength.rationale: A real political word that fits the congressional customer, but many unrelated organizations share it (Startup Caucus, Future Caucus, CaucusRoom), and only one launch coverage item from June 2025 was found.

outcome_analysis: Caucus joined YC in Spring 2025 with a founder who had already sold a legislative AI startup to FiscalNote and a Yale trained technical co-founder. Databases show only a small pre-seed total. YC now lists it as Inactive, but no source gives a cause, so the reason for the stall is not public and no failure factor is assigned.
notes: Pre-seed round rests on a single aggregator (VCBacked). Competitors left empty on purpose: vendor pages found for Fireside Federal, Indigov and iConstituent were undated, and the launch post names no rival, so none could be listed with a source dated near the batch. The cause of the Inactive status was searched and not found. Education of Farahani not found.
